title.rendered: Josh Harford Alliance Party Campaign Launch

content.rendered:
Join the Alliance Party at 6pm Saturday 10 October at Trades Hall on Vivian St for the official launch of Josh Harford’s campaign for Wellington North.

Come and hear from Josh about the progress of his campaign thus far, and what he would seek to change were he to be elected. There will also be other speakers announced in due course.

If you are looking to get involved in Alliance’s campaign in Wellington, this event is a good opportunity to meet the crew and find out more about how you can contribute.

Complimentary refreshments will be available through the evening.

View the Facebook event

party list

Meet the candidates ↓

7 October 2026

The Alliance Party has announced its party list and electorate candidates for the 7 November 2026 general election.

The line-up brings together frontline workers, community representatives, professionals, trade unionists and small businesspeople to challenge the political status quo.

Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot says the candidates offer voters a clear democratic socialist choice in an election dominated by “inertia and managed decline”.

“Working people across New Zealand are bearing the brunt of runaway living costs, deteriorating public services and housing insecurity, while wealth and power continue to be concentrated in the hands of a few,” says Mr Billot.

“The Alliance was built to break the two-party establishment. We are not running to tinker around the edges or manage austerity. Our candidates are active in their communities and workplaces, ready to fight for public ownership, workers’ rights and social justice.”

title.rendered: A Commitment to Peace: Alliance Party Releases Foreign Affairs, Defence, and International Relations Policy

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has released its Foreign Affairs, Defence, and International Relations Policy, a rebuke of the USA-centric philosophy which has skewed Aotearoa New Zealand’s international relations for the better part of eighty years. Foreign Affairs and Defence spokesperson Josh Harford said that the policy is designed to cement the country’s independence in a fractious world:

“We are increasingly moving away from a unipolar world order determined by the capriciousness of American foreign policy. It is time to forge our own path, with the independence and security of our Pacific region front and centre.”

The policy emphasises internationalism, non-alignment, disarmament, and decolonisation. It includes support for a strong United Nations and the South Pacific Nuclear Free Zone. It also reaffirms the Alliance Party’s commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals.

Mr. Harford said that one basic tenet of the policy is the right to self-determination:

“Too many people around the world are subjected to rule through force. Whether it is nations under dictatorship, or independent people subjugated by another nation. We would use our voice to draw attention to these injustices. In the Middle East, we must demand self-determination for Palestinians and the right to return to their homeland.”

“The Alliance Party is proud of New Zealand’s record as an internationalist nation. As a founding member of the United Nations, UNESCO, and much more, we have a proven track record as a fighter for peace, diplomacy, and stability around the world. We are a proud and committed advocate of the Sustainable Development Goals, and we have the opportunity to build on this record into the future.”

He also took aim at the brutal cycle of debt which he says cripples the Global South:

“Developing nations should not be trapped in cycles of debt repayment that prevent them from providing basic services, investing in their people, or developing sustainable economies. Global South debt is a leading cause of corruption, poverty, and state failure.”

“National destitution is often a direct result of colonialism and resource extraction. Developed nations, especially those who participated in exploiting other countries, have a responsibility to cancel their foreign aid debts as a form of reparation. We see the necessary link between economic and national sovereignty. One without the other is illusory, and that is as true for Aotearoa New Zealand as it is for anywhere else.”

Mr. Harford also pointed to existing US military and intelligence infrastructure in New Zealand as undermining national sovereignty:

“As we speak, our country is providing military and political intelligence that the United States uses or provides to other powerful states, enabling atrocities around the world. Tangimoana, Waihopai, Black Birch, and Wellington’s FBI Office are used to advance the hegemony of another state, with no regard for our own national interest. We pledge to immediately terminate intelligence sharing, with a view to fully demilitarising these facilities.”

Download the full Foreign Affairs, Defence, and International Relations Policy (PDF, 6 pages)

title.rendered: Time to Take Back Our Power: Alliance Launches “Reverse Privatisation” Plan

content.rendered:
Decades after the fire sale of New Zealand’s national assets in the 1980s and 1990s, the Alliance has announced a comprehensive plan to restore and protect public ownership of essential services and strategic infrastructure.

The Alliance today launched its Public Ownership and Economic Democracy Policy, a “reverse privatisation” programme to progressively buy back strategic assets that were sold and protect those that remain publicly owned. The programme would be prioritised by strategic importance, with the Crown purchasing assets at fair value where appropriate.

Alliance Party leader Victor Billot says the goal is to build a resilient New Zealand where people control their own destiny.

“Households are cutting back on heating, infrastructure is creaking, and too many essential services are treated as cash machines for private interests. This is the legacy of the failed neoliberal sell-off of New Zealand.”

Mr Billot says it is unacceptable that many New Zealanders are struggling to stay afloat from week to week.

He says a key policy is to bring the electricity system as a whole under public ownership and control, covering generation, transmission, distribution and retail, with the goal of affordable, sustainable energy for households and local industry.

Mr Billot says the Alliance would invest in publicly owned KiwiRail, move Air New Zealand from majority Crown ownership to full public ownership, and progressively restore public ownership of strategically important ports where privatisation or corporatisation has undermined public control.

“The Alliance Party identifies the State Owned Enterprises Act as an unmitigated failure. Turning public goods and services into commercial entities for privatised profit was absurd in 1986 and it’s absurd today. We will repeal and replace this legislation so that the people of this country have the infrastructure they built and paid for work for them – not corporate shareholders.”

The Alliance would keep public water services and infrastructure in public ownership and bring monopoly telecommunications infrastructure into public ownership, including the “last mile” connections to homes and businesses.

The Alliance would create KiwiWorks, a Ministry of Works for the 21st Century, to build state housing and infrastructure, develop construction capacity and create jobs. It would also establish a Ministry of Development and a publicly owned Development Bank, and keep Kiwibank in public ownership.

Works councils would be introduced in larger enterprises, and workers would be represented on the boards of major public enterprises. The Official Information Act would be extended to Crown-controlled listed companies.

Mr Billot says the Alliance is committed to giving workers a voice in the enterprises their labour builds.

To protect economic resilience, the Crown would have a right of first refusal, depending on fiscal viability, to acquire businesses in identified critical industries facing sale or liquidation. Where necessary, it could operate them publicly or work with employees to support cooperative buyouts.

Download the full Public Ownership and Economic Democracy Policy (PDF, 9 pages)

title.rendered: Open, Not Owned: Alliance Party Announces Trade Policy

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has announced the first installment in its Trade Policy, which will modernise Aotearoa New Zealand’s international trade regime, protect local industries, and take a stand for human rights around the world.

Alliance Party trade spokesperson and candidate for Wellington North, Josh Harford, says international trade is rapidly becoming a race to the bottom.

“The craven, unrestrained obsession with maximising profits serves only to destroy local industry and bring misery on populations elsewhere in the world. Manufacturing in Aotearoa New Zealand once comprised one-quarter of all economic activity. Now, it is barely one-tenth.”

The policy includes protectionist policies around manufacturing and industry to support economic sovereignty.

“In the past three years, we have seen factory after factory close their doors, usually in order to shift production overseas. This has damaged the economies of our regional centres, worsened unemployment, and deepened generational poverty for many. We cannot be a fully-employed nation when we ship so much economic potential offshore,” Mr Harford says.

The policy includes guidelines for fair and managed trade, rather than free trade.

“Fair trade goes hand in hand with equality. Sweatshops around the world employ women and children in forced labour conditions, exploiting poverty conditions and societal barriers.”

Mr Harford says the Alliance is not opposed to international trade, and recognises that Aotearoa New Zealand is a small market often at the end of a long and expansive supply chain.

“We do not believe in shutting off from the world, but right now we profit from modern slavery, outsource environmentally damaging manufacturing that we still rely on, all while undermining our economic and political sovereignty.”

“We believe in a diversified local economy: one that will take measures to protect critical industry, keep it on shore, and expand it,” Mr Harford says.

Mr Harford took aim at existing regulations:

“We have a very weak trade framework, designed to maximise corporate profits with little regard for either domestic industry or human rights. Without a humanitarian approach to international trade and robust modern slavery legislation, we are rapidly becoming a global outlier.”

“This government has shown great vigour in fast-tracking legislation and using urgency for policies that harm Aotearoa New Zealand. The Alliance Party would bring that gusto to updating our modern slavery legislation and cracking down on exploitation in our trade settings.”

Mr. Harford also observed that humanitarian trade policy benefits domestic workers just as much as those overseas:

“By cracking down on bad actors and unethical practices, we remove the financial incentive to exploit. This will help to restore industry and manufacturing on our shores. We can be a powerhouse of industry, but only if we have the right settings in place to protect those industries.”

Download the full Trade Policy (PDF, 5 pages)

excerpt.rendered: Alliance proposes fair and managed trade to support local industry, protect working conditions and retain democratic control of the economy.

title.rendered: Alliance Party: Redistribute Power, Honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi, Move Forward in Unity

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has released its Te Tiriti o Waitangi, Democracy, and Constitutional policy which aims to redistribute power to ordinary people by advancing constitutional transformation with Te Tiriti o Waitangi at the centre.

Download the full policy (PDF, 9 pages) ↓

Alliance Party president and constitutional spokesperson Tom Roud says the policy builds on the party’s commitment to redistribution of more than wealth alone.

“Our policies tend to deal with immediate, material needs of ordinary Kiwis with an emphasis on the redistribution of wealth in this country. Redistribution of wealth without a rebalance of power would represent a gilded cage for working people, so we want to go further,” he says.

The policy is built on the principles of popular sovereignty, participatory democracy, social justice, and upholding Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

“The Alliance Party and the workers movement in general have a proud history of standing with Māori in their struggle with the Crown to address the criminal attacks on mana motuhake, tino rangatiratanga, and breaches of Te Tiriti o Waitangi. Our re-established party pays respect to our own whakapapa, and our previous relationship with the political party Mana Motuhake has provided us with a legacy of sound policy that respects Māori rights,” Mr Roud says.

On democratic issues the policy supports lowering the threshold for entering parliament and establishing processes for the recall of elected candidates by their electors.

“We are proud to be a radically democratic party that would see a system where no vote is wasted, where power does not become entrenched through custom and practice, and where elected officials are not given a few years of power without any recourse for voters to oust them if they so wish.”

“Accountability can’t just happen every few years at the ballot box, it is a relationship that our politicians must be expected to maintain. If they can’t manage that, voters should be able to remove them from office,” Mr Roud says.

The Alliance supports advancing a written constitution, designed by the people of Aotearoa New Zealand through participatory democracy, and enshrining the constitutional status of Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

“The Matike Mai report was an enormous step forward for a serious constitutional conversation in this country. Tangata whenua have provided a framework, and now the rest of the country must come along for the conversation.”

“These are not easy subjects to cover, they take courage and a spirit of kotahitanga (unity) if we are going to come into our own as a country.”

“I am a republican, my neighbour may be a constitutional monarchist, how will we reconcile this? What would ‘the Crown’ come to mean in our existing legislation if we went down a republican route? How do we ensure we honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi in any new constitutional arrangement? Is an upper chamber undemocratic, or a necessary check on power?” Mr Roud says.

“Like almost everyone in this country I am not an expert on these issues. Regardless, the Alliance Party knows these are questions that will only become more and more central to the future of the country. It is time for Aotearoa New Zealand to decide who we want to be, and work through any nervousness and fear about that together. Tūwhitia te hopo, mairangatia te angitū: feel the fear, and do it anyway.”

For more information contact Alliance Party president and constitutional spokesperson Tom Roud on 0278667683 or president@allianceparty.nz

title.rendered: Alliance Party Commits to 65 Retirement Age, Funding Aged Care Support, Supercharging KiwiSaver

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has released its Retirement and Aged Care Policy, which keeps the pension universal, lifts the couple rate to the highest level the law allows, and commits to ending the asset test for rest home care.

Download the full policy (PDF, 6 pages) ↓

The Alliance’s health spokesperson, Ethan Gullery, says too many people spend their whole working life saving for retirement only to end up losing their independence.

“People spend their whole life working and saving to own their home, and then they end up having to spend it on care before the state will help.”

Under current policy, a person is only entitled to government funding for rest home care once their assets, including the family home, have fallen to $300,811. With care costing around $1,500 a week, someone whose home and other assets are worth $650,000 would pay for about four and a half years of care before the state contributes.

Mr Gullery says Super already shows a better way to do it.

“We don’t means test Super. Everyone gets it, and that’s a big part of why it’s survived. Long-term care should work on the same basis.”

The policy includes a long-term approach to supercharge KiwiSaver into a true superannuation fund, completing the promise of the 1974 Superannuation Act. The first step includes a $10,000 endowment to new KiwiSaver accounts, ringfenced for retirement or terminal illness.

“The repeal of the Superannuation Act in 1975 was one of the worst economic decisions ever made in this country, and we have been playing catch up as a nation ever since. The best time to set up a superannuation system that works was decades ago – the second best time is now. As no one else will take up the mantle of forward-thinking people like Norman Kirk, the Alliance Party will do so proudly.”

“Our changes to KiwiSaver will take decades to bear fruit in full, but will ensure future generations are supported to live in dignity and security through their retirement.”

The Alliance Party also promises to increase New Zealand Superannuation for couples to 72.5 per cent of the after-tax average wage. Parliament put that upper limit in the law. The Alliance would use it, and adjust Super every quarter.

The policy also:

  • Keeps the age of entitlement for Super at 65
  • Funds independent advocates to support older people dealing with agencies and providers
  • Sets up a dedicated Ministry for Senior Citizens

“We are a workers’ party,” says Mr Gullery. “And after working most of their lives, workers deserve the security of knowing that they can enjoy a healthy and happy retirement without the fear of financial insecurity.”

For more information contact Alliance Party health spokesperson and Christchurch East candidate Ethan Gullery on 021 318 633 or ethan.gullery@allianceparty.nz

excerpt.rendered: A universal pension, a higher couple rate, an end to the asset test for rest home care, and a $10,000 endowment to new KiwiSaver accounts.

title.rendered: The Right to a Roof: Our Housing Policy

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party is proud to unveil an ambitious, modern housing policy designed to bring our national housing infrastructure into the twenty-first century. Alliance Party housing spokesperson and candidate for Palmerston North, Joshua Moss, said the policy was founded primarily on one overarching principle:

Download the full Housing Policy (PDF, 6 pages)

“Every human being has the right to a warm, safe, and secure home at a fair price. Through four decades of neglect, privatisation, and inaction we have failed to maintain or improve the provision of public housing. We will reverse this trend.”

The centrepiece of the Alliance policy is a five-year housing plan: a massive public building programme led by Kāinga Ora, alongside a newly established Ministry of Works, to build the homes and infrastructure Aotearoa New Zealand needs.

“We will clear the social housing register, while creating decent jobs in construction and building high-quality homes that last,” Mr Moss said.

The Alliance policy caps social housing rent at 25 percent of income, and establishes state backed mortgages and co-ownership models to help working people get into housing.

“Our economy has been reliant on property speculation for too long, but the commodification of housing does enormous harm to our communities. The Alliance believes housing is a public good, and will implement lending criteria that favours owner-occupiers while discouraging property speculators.”

“We won’t build a productive economy by buying and selling houses to one another. The state must intervene in the housing market significantly to provide a real reset, and encourage investment into higher productivity sectors,” Mr Moss said.

“It’s time we started thinking of housing more like manners at a potluck – everyone gets a plate before anyone has seconds.”

For more information contact Alliance Party housing spokesperson and Palmerston North candidate Joshua Moss on 0273187235, or joshua.moss@allianceparty.nz

Download the full Housing Policy (PDF, 6 pages)

title.rendered: Alliance Party Plan to Eliminate Child Poverty

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has further elaborated on its social security and welfare policies, with a focus on the elimination of child poverty.

Download the full policy (PDF, 4 pages) ↓

Alliance social security spokesperson and West Coast-Tasman candidate Sara Dyatlova Murphy said the policy provides greater detail on the previously announced Universal Child Benefit, with a broader social justice focus.

“No child should grow up in poverty in Aotearoa New Zealand, and the fact is that children are not being paid poverty benefits or poverty wages – that happens to their caregivers” Ms Dyatlova-Murphy said.

The Alliance policy emphasises the status of children as citizens in their own right, not merely the dependants of adults. Ms Dyatlova-Murphy said all government policy must consider the impact on children as members of our society with their own rights and interests.

“The same level of care given to the impact on women, on the environment, on tangata whenua, when auditing government policy should also apply to some of the most vulnerable in our community who can not directly impact government through voting – children and youth.”

Ms Dyatlova-Murphy says the policy has been shaped by the work of the Child Poverty Action Group, whose research has kept child poverty on the national agenda for more than thirty years.

“CPAG have spent decades documenting what poverty does to children in this country, and making the case for change when it wasn’t popular. Their work has shaped our thinking, and we’re grateful for it.”

CPAG’s 2026 election manifesto challenges every party to commit to solutions for children. The Alliance policy is our answer to that challenge.

“There is no reason a child in this country should grow up in poverty and insecurity. Children have a claim over the shared resources of our society, and until all children are provided with what they need to thrive we will never realise our full potential as a nation.”

“If we care for the next generation, every New Zealander will benefit.”

For more information contact Alliance Party Social Security spokesperson and West Coast – Tasman candidate Sara Dyatlova–Murphy on 022 4147223

title.rendered: Justice Policy: “Three Strikes and into Treatment”

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has released its 2026 Justice Policy, built around preventing harm, repairing it, and standing with victims.

Download the full Justice Policy (PDF, 8 pages)

Alliance Party justice spokesperson and Ilam candidate Courtney Fraser says the state of the courts and prisons is not an accident but a policy choice.

“It’s hard to talk about criminal justice without talking about policy, because where we find ourselves today with incarceration, the lack of rehabilitation, and the lack of access to services, is down to public policy.”

“Our criminal law is still built around punishing the people who offend, and there is far too little for the victims of crime.”

“Underinvestment in housing, work, training, and education over the last forty years has led to a social crisis, and our courts are where that crisis ends up.”

Ms Fraser says the Alliance policy tackles the causes of offending through secure housing, decent work, education and training, healthcare, and mental health and addiction services.

The policy establishes habilitation centres as an alternative to prison, particularly for young people, and brings back Community Care Orders as a sentencing option.

It places restorative justice at the centre of appropriate responses to offending, supports marae-based processes where appropriate, and properly resources iwi and Māori organisations to provide rehabilitation and restorative programmes.

A properly resourced Victim/Criminal Compensation Board will oversee financial, physical and other support for victims of crime.

Ms Fraser says the Alliance will review legal aid with the aim of a comprehensive, publicly funded system of legal assistance, including expanded legal aid, sustainable resourcing for Community Law Centres, and an enhanced Public Defence Service, so that no one is denied justice because they are poor.

Prisons will be publicly owned and operated, and the Alliance opposes private prisons. Reflecting its principle that no person or corporation is above the law, the Alliance will also reinstate the right to sue corporations or individuals over damage caused by emissions-related climate change effects.

“We’re all in this together on these tiny, faraway islands. We must close the gaps in our systems so none of us are left behind.”

“The best thing we can do for victims is stop making new ones. Where the current approach is three strikes and out, ours is three strikes and into treatment.”

The policy rests on six principles: prevent rather than simply punish; rehabilitate rather than abandon; restore where possible rather than simply incarcerate; support victims rather than abandoning them; guarantee access to justice regardless of wealth; and protect rights by holding everyone, including government and corporations, accountable under the law.

For more information, contact Alliance Party justice spokesperson and Ilam candidate Courtney Fraser on 027 470 8900

excerpt.rendered: The Alliance’s 2026 Justice Policy focuses on preventing harm, rehabilitation, support for victims and access to justice regardless of wealth.

title.rendered: Small Is Beautiful! Backing Small Business, Local Enterprise, and Cooperatives

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has announced its Small Business, Local Enterprise, and Cooperative Development policy, with a strategy to protect independent operators, raise working standards, and curb the dominance of corporate monopolies.

Download the full Small Business, Local Enterprise, and Cooperative Development policy (PDF, 6 pages)

Alliance Party small business spokesperson Anna Knight says New Zealand’s small businesses, family farms, independent contractors, and cooperatives are essential to a democratic, resilient economy.

“Small businesses keep wealth in local circulation and communities sustained but are currently bearing the brunt of an unfair economic system.”

Ms Knight says small businesses suffer from a race to the bottom when it comes to wages, hours, and conditions, both for their workers, and for owner-operators who are under immense pressure.

The policy launch follows a spike in insolvencies, with 2025 company liquidations reaching levels not seen since the aftermath of the 2010 Global Financial Crisis.

About half of New Zealand’s small businesses close within five years, and fewer than thirty percent survive a decade.

“Insolvency doesn’t happen overnight, the so-called ‘failure curve’ creeps up and is the result of many forces. We want to attack these at the root.”

“We want to reset this dynamic and ensure everyone in a small enterprise gets a fair deal.”

Ms Knight says to reverse this trend, the Alliance will restructure the tax base so the burden falls on concentrated, accumulated wealth rather than productive small enterprises.

The Alliance will overhaul competition law to break up corporate market power, with a focus on sectors like the supermarket duopoly, which extracts an estimated $430 million annually in excess profits. Suppliers can’t negotiate easily with just two buyers, and small retailers simply can’t compete.

A publicly owned development bank will be established to deliver low-cost financing for local enterprise, backed by community resource hubs and an Applied Technology Programme to foster domestic tech sovereignty.

The Alliance will create a framework to support employee buy-outs with targeted development in regional economies.

Minimum employment protections will be extended to contractors to stop wage undercutting, alongside mandatory maximum payment terms and public reporting on payment times for large corporate buyers.

Ms Knight says it is important to remember that all wage-earning is essentially a credit given to your employer, and, by the same token, a small business should not be providing an interest-free loan to a company many times its size.

“Our goal is not simply to grow business balance sheets, but to decentralise economic power so it directly serves local communities, workers, and families.”

For more information contact Alliance small business spokesperson Anna Knight on 02040728703

excerpt.rendered: The Alliance proposes low-cost finance, stronger competition rules, support for cooperatives and fairer payment terms for small businesses and local enterprise.

title.rendered: 52 Weeks’ Paid Parental Leave in Our Gender Equality Plan

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has announced a comprehensive women, gender equality, and economic security policy including at least fifty-two weeks’ paid parental leave, a Universal Child Benefit, and stronger enforcement of pay equity.

Download the full Women, Gender Equality, and Economic Security policy (PDF, 8 pages)

Alliance Party national secretary and gender equality spokesperson Sionainn Byrnes says formal rights alone cannot overcome the barriers that prevent many women from participating fully in society.

“Legal equality is necessary, but it is not enough. Women need the economic security, public services, and practical support that allow them to exercise their rights and participate fully in society.”

The Alliance policy would provide at least fifty-two weeks’ paid parental leave to eligible workers, including casual, seasonal, and part-time workers. Its parental-leave arrangements would recognise that caring responsibilities are shared by parents and caregivers.

A Universal Child Benefit would be paid directly to the principal caregiver for every child and indexed to movements in average weekly earnings.

Ms Byrnes says care work is economically and socially valuable, and it needs to be treated as such.

“Raising children and caring for whānau should not push people into poverty, reduce their retirement security, or limit their opportunities at work. Properly recognising care work is non-negotiable.”

The policy would also establish a Pay Equity Bureau to monitor and enforce pay equity. It provides for strengthened Employment Equity legislation, collective and class-based claims where discrimination is systemic, greater wage transparency, and comparisons between female-dominated and male-dominated occupations to assess work of equal value.

Ms Byrnes says women remain concentrated in work that has been undervalued and underpaid.

“People working in care and support roles, and other female-dominated occupations, deserve proper recognition and fair pay.”

The Alliance would support accessible, affordable, and high-quality childcare, including non-profit and publicly supported services for parents working shifts, evenings, nights, and weekends.

The policy also affirms bodily autonomy and reproductive healthcare. It supports free, safe, and accessible abortion services throughout Aotearoa, universal access to contraception through the public health system, comprehensive age-appropriate sexuality education, and an informed consent model of gender-affirming care.

Other commitments include secure, long-term funding for women’s refuges and specialist services, safe and affordable housing for women fleeing violence, gender-impact assessments of government decisions, and progressive movement towards a thirty-five-hour working week without loss of income.

Ms Byrnes says the policy recognises the particular rights and circumstances of wāhine Māori under Te Tiriti o Waitangi, as well as the different barriers experienced by Pasifika women, disabled women, older women, migrant women, lesbian and trans women, sole parents, and women facing poverty or insecure housing.

“Women’s equality must mean economic independence, control over our own bodies, freedom from violence, and an equal voice in the decisions that shape our lives.”

For more information contact Alliance Party national secretary and gender equality spokesperson Sionainn Byrnes on 022 060 6549

title.rendered: Our Plan to Rebuild Universal Social Security

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party will end benefit sanctions, individualise social security entitlements, and establish a Universal Benefit as the foundation of a new social security system under its 2026 election policy.

Download the full welfare, family and social security policy (PDF, 4 pages) ↓

The Alliance will also introduce universal payments for children and families, end unnecessary benefit stand-down periods, and replace the current high-compliance welfare model with a high-trust system based on adequate incomes, dignity, and universal entitlement.

Alliance social security spokesperson and West Coast–Tasman candidate Sara Dyatlova–Murphy said the policy represented a fundamental change in how New Zealand treats people who need income support.

“Social security must stop people falling into poverty, not punish them once they get there.

“Losing a job, becoming ill or disabled, caring for a family member, or needing help while studying are ordinary risks and responsibilities. We need to ensure people have security when those things happen.”

The Universal Benefit would be set at a level reflecting reasonable average living costs and providing an adequate standard of living.

Entitlements would be individualised, so a person’s access to support would no longer depend on their partner’s income or circumstances.

Ms Dyatlova–Murphy said the Alliance would also abolish sanctions, unnecessary stand-down periods, and welfare debt and debt-recovery practices that push people further into hardship.

“Taking money away from someone who already cannot afford food, rent, or power does not solve unemployment or poverty. It simply makes a bad situation worse.”

The policy would write off existing beneficiary debt owed to the Ministry of Social Development and replace recoverable assistance for urgent needs with grants where appropriate.

Core social security payments would be indexed quarterly to either average weekly earnings or the Consumer Price Index, whichever produced the greater increase.

Families would receive a Universal Early Years Benefit for every child under three, followed by a Universal Child Benefit from age three until sixteen, regardless of family income or relationship status.

“Universal child support recognises that helping families raise healthy, secure children is a responsibility shared across society,” Ms Dyatlova–Murphy says.

The policy would also expand support for people living with illness or disability, provide direct payments for family members and other primary carers, and develop a caregiver wage recognising the value of unpaid care.

Students and trainees would receive a universal student income, independent of parental income and set at a liveable level equivalent to the unemployment benefit.

“Everyone should have the security to participate fully in their family, their community, and society, whatever their circumstances.”

For more information contact Alliance Party Social Security spokesperson and West Coast–Tasman candidate Sara Dyatlova–Murphy on 022 4147223.

title.rendered: Hon. Matt Robson – NZ First Immigration Proposals Prove ‘Patriotism Is the Last Refuge of a Scoundrel’

content.rendered:
Alliance Party media release
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Monday 14 September 2026

Alliance Party immigration spokesperson Hon. Matt Robson says New Zealand First leader Winston Peters seems determined to prove Samuel Johnson’s dictum that “patriotism is the last refuge of a scoundrel”.

Matt Robson says New Zealand First’s recent attacks on migrants are cynical electioneering that wraps the anti-democratic politics of bigotry in the flag.

“It is an old and ugly trick for politicians to seek votes through migrant-bashing policies.

“Mr Peters is introducing Trumpian, MAGA-style politics into the election campaign as he tries to distance himself from his role in the failed policies of the coalition government.

“Equal legal rights are a New Zealand value. Policies that strip fundamental appeal rights from migrants and refugees do not uphold that principle.”

Matt Robson says it is not a New Zealand value to deny citizenship to children of New Zealand residents.

“What comes next for New Zealand First – identity badges for migrants and refugees to be worn at all times?

“Why should taxpaying permanent residents have to wait ten years before being able to apply for citizenship? What evidence is there that this group of New Zealand residents is somehow disloyal?”

Matt Robson says former Prime Minister Michael Joseph Savage was a permanent resident without New Zealand citizenship.

“Was he disloyal to New Zealand?

“These MAGA-inspired, anti-migrant rants are the product of divisive and cruel politics that should be swept out of Parliament at the coming election.”

Matt Robson says the Alliance will campaign for positive not divisive immigration policies.

ENDS

For more information, contact Alliance Party immigration spokesperson Hon. Matt Robson on 021 909 936.

Editorial Note – About Hon. Matt Robson

Mr Robson is a former MP for the Alliance and Progressive parties, and was a Cabinet minister in the 1999–2002 Labour–Alliance coalition government. He is co-producer of the recent documentary Last Man Standing, on the life and times of Jim Anderton. Matt works as an immigration lawyer in Auckland and is actively supporting the relaunched Alliance Party.

title.rendered: Our National Strategy on Transport

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has announced its transport policy focused on delivering economic participation, community wellbeing, and national supply chain resilience during climate emergencies and global disruption.

Download the full transport policy (PDF, 5 pages) ↓

The Alliance will establish a 100-percent publicly owned, integrated freight and passenger network in which coastal shipping and rail serve as the twin backbones of domestic long-distance freight.

The Alliance is committed to public ownership of other strategic transport assets such as ports, aviation and transit.

Alliance Party transport spokesperson and candidate for Banks Peninsula, Kyle Turnbull, says New Zealand cannot keep relying on road freight domestically, or on global shipping companies for exporting and importing.

“New Zealand is a remote island nation and a relatively small market on the global stage. An integrated and efficient transport system for moving goods domestically and internationally is essential for our economic sovereignty and national security.”

Mr Turnbull says recent disruptions to global supply chains have already shown that New Zealand is exposed and vulnerable.

“Whether the threat is the closure of a key shipping lane such as the Strait of Hormuz, a global pandemic, or extreme weather events, New Zealand needs resilient supply chains.”

“By setting up rail and coastal shipping as the twin backbones of freight, we will build a resilient network that can respond to natural disasters, reduce carbon emissions, and move freight off roads.”

In the maritime transport sector, Alliance would establish a State shipping line as part of a wider domestic and regional shipping plan, and implement a national port strategy.

The Alliance proposes an increase in funding for public transport, and the repeal of procurement requirements that force local government into corporatised models of public transport provision.

Mr Turnbull says public transport works the best when it is well run, properly funded, and affordable, so that people from all walks of life use it as the first choice for their daily commute.

“That means it needs to be run as a public service, integrated nationally, and made as widely available as possible – not just in the cities but also in the regions – so people can get where they need to go.”

“Our upgrade of commuter rail across the country will provide jobs and reconnect regional New Zealand and small towns to the wider economy.”

“The neglect of our regions is evident in the lack of infrastructure, and the absence of a plan for regional economic development. It is a decades-long scandal. The Alliance is committed to changing that, and our transport policy will form a key part of that change.”

For more information contact Alliance Party transport spokesperson and candidate for Banks Peninsula Kyle Turnbull on 0224685436.

title.rendered: Our Health Policy Eliminates Costs for GP Visits, Dental, Optical, and Audiology Services

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has announced its health policy, which includes the elimination of costs for GP visits, dental, optical, and audiology services.

Download the full health policy (PDF, 7 pages) ↓

In order to achieve this, the policy creates the Community Health Service (CHS) as the main funding and logistical service to bring primary and allied health services into the public service.

Existing services have the option to join the CHS, with the CHS covering the costs of the practice, including rent, payroll, administration, and information technology. The staff would be employed by the CHS.

For the patients, there would be very few changes in the short term. The CHS would take over the practice, but the patients would still see the same doctors, and it would still be the same clinic. The biggest change would be that appointments would be free.

The CHS would also change how the system is funded. Primary care funding moves beyond capitation, with money allocated for things like chronic care clinics. Community and hospital services would then be funded as one system, so that keeping someone out of hospital counts as a win rather than a hospital losing the funding for treating them.

Alliance health spokesperson and candidate for Christchurch East, Ethan Gullery, says this is a positive step towards a fully integrated health care system.

“Right now, we treat the system as a bunch of disconnected pieces, funding hospitals one way and funding clinics another. We know that the best care is earliest care, but the focus is on the secondary care system. The Alliance wants to change that.”

In the Alliance's CHS model, community and primary care workers would be equal to their secondary care colleagues in pay and would come under the existing collective agreements. Māori health providers would keep the option to remain independent, with full funding and pay equity for their staff either way.

“A fragmented system means a fragmented workforce, negotiating with many employers, trying to get the bare minimum.”

Mr Gullery says this change is the shakeup needed.

“We have heard from GPs and GP practices, and it has become obvious in those conversations that very few people become doctors in order to end up being small businesspeople. Not only that but they are running small businesses in an area where the economics stopped being favourable decades ago. The Alliance is the only party willing to stand up and say the entire system needs to change.”

excerpt.rendered: Alliance proposes a public Community Health Service with free GP, dental, optical and audiology care, team-based prevention and workforce pay parity.

title.rendered: Public Power, Clean Water, Polluters Pay: A Just Transition in Our Environment Policy

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party says Aotearoa New Zealand should stop treating economic growth as the main measure of national progress, and instead judge government policy by whether it improves people’s lives while protecting the environment.

The proposal is at the core of the Alliance’s new Environmental, Climate, and Sustainable Economy Policy, which sets out a vision for a “cooperative, ecological economy”.

Read the full policy

Environmental, Climate, and Sustainable Economy Policy
PDF, 11 pages, 211 KB

Download policy PDF

Alliance environment spokesperson and Christchurch Central candidate Greg Byrnes says environmental and economic policy can no longer be treated as separate issues.

“An economy can be growing on paper while natural resources are depleted, ecosystems are damaged, and communities carry the wider costs,” says Mr Byrnes.

“We need to ask whether people are better off, and are we leaving a healthy environment for future generations?”

The Alliance proposes moving towards a Genuine Progress Index, or GPI, as a central measure of national progress, alongside environmental auditing and true-cost accounting.

The GPI would take account of environmental health, public health and wellbeing, social equality, economic security, public services, unpaid caring and community work, and the interests of future generations.

Mr Byrnes says government decisions need to be judged on their real social and environmental consequences, not simply on whether they increase Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

The policy also proposes:

  • a polluter-pays principle requiring those responsible for environmental damage to meet the full cost of prevention and repair;
  • the “right to repair” and a move towards a zero-waste, circular economy;
  • 100 percent public ownership of electricity generation, transmission, distribution, and retail with a focus on renewables;
  • replacing the Emissions Trading Scheme with a carbon tax, with revenue directed towards renewable energy, public transport, and emissions reduction;
  • keeping water infrastructure and services in public ownership, with stronger controls on water pollution; and
  • prohibiting mining in national parks, conservation areas, and other protected public land.

Mr Byrnes says deteriorating freshwater quality including rivers and groundwater shows why urgent environmental action is necessary.

He says environmental change must not come at the expense of workers and communities.

“We know parts of our economy still depend on finite and extractive resources, but multinational corporations cannot be trusted to look after either the environment or their workers when those industries reach the end of the road.”

“As part of a Just Transition, the government must retrain and redeploy workers, invest in alternative industries and support communities affected by change.”

The Alliance proposes bringing extractive industries into public ownership as they are progressively wound down, with revenue used for environmental restoration, worker retraining, redeployment, and regional investment.

Mr Byrnes says the basic principle of the Alliance policy is straightforward.

“Our economy must serve people and communities, and it has to operate within the ecological limits of the planet.”

For more information, contact Alliance Environment Spokesperson and Christchurch Central candidate Greg Byrnes on mobile 021 0245 5398

About Greg Byrnes

Mr Byrnes is a former regional councillor on Environment Canterbury (2022–2025), and was chair of the Regional Biodiversity & Biosecurity Committee during 2023.

He is a professional environmentalist and spent twelve years as general manager of Tūhaitara Coastal Park, a 750 ha coastal wetland and dune area in North Canterbury.

Alliance environment spokesperson and candidate for Christchurch Central.

title.rendered: Full Employment and a 35-Hour Week in Our Workers’ Rights Policy

content.rendered:
Alliance Party Media Release
Monday, 7 September 2026, 7:58 am

The Alliance Party has released its policy for employment relations and workers’ rights.

Read the full policy

Workers’ Rights and Employment Policy
PDF, 10 pages, 195 KB

Download policy PDF

Alliance employment relations spokesperson and candidate for Selwyn, Jesse Luke, says the policy is “pro-worker, pro-union, and pro-jobs.”

“Working people must be able to protect and advance their interests collectively. For 40 years trade unions and workers’ rights have been under attack, driving a race to the bottom in our wages and conditions.”

He says the Alliance policy includes full employment, a 35-hour working week with no loss in pay, five weeks of annual leave, workplace democracy, and a broad restoration of the right to strike.

“Currently, the employer holds the purse strings and the worker sells their labour to them. To have a fair go, workers need the right to withdraw their labour.”

“No one takes such action lightly, and a loss of pay is a significant sacrifice, but New Zealand has highly restrictive strike laws. The Alliance will change that.”

Mr Luke says the policy sets the Alliance apart because it is not simply about improving wages and conditions, but about rebalancing economic power between employers and workers.

“The Alliance does not accept workplaces being run like dictatorships when people spend such a large part of their lives at work. Workers have a genuine interest in the successful and fair operation of their workplaces, and they deserve a real say in the decisions that affect them.”

The Alliance policy proposes Work Councils in workplaces with more than 50 workers and elected Worker Directors in enterprises employing more than 250 workers.

The Alliance policy includes greater support and resourcing of the Employment Relations Authority and the Labour Inspectorate, alongside establishing a Workplace Safety Authority.

“Exploitation, breaches of employment law, and dangerous workplace practices will be taken seriously. We will treat wage theft as theft. We will advance legislation for corporate homicide and corporate manslaughter.”

“There must be no more deaths on the waterfront, in forestry, and in other high-risk industries. Employers that breach employment and workplace safety law must face effective enforcement and meaningful penalties.”

title.rendered: Our Tax Plan Makes First $20,000 Income Tax-Free, Funded by Wealth Tax

content.rendered:
Alliance Party Media Release
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Sunday 6 September 2026

The Alliance Party has unveiled its tax package, proposing to make the first $20,000 of every person’s income completely tax-free. Under the proposed scale, an everyday worker earning $65,000 would keep an extra $2,408 a year.

Download the policy documents

  • Tax Justice and Cost of Living PolicyPDF, 4 pages, 135 KB
  • Tax Policy Costings: The NumbersPDF, 5 pages, 195 KB

The package combines taxes on wealth, realised capital gains, and financial transactions with a 30% corporate tax rate and a rebalanced income tax scale. The Alliance’s costings estimate a net revenue surplus in both the first term and at year 10.

  • $20,000 Tax-Free Threshold: Universal, automatic, and permanent relief. All earners below the $178,150 break-even point pay less income tax. Proposed upper rates are 34% from $78,100 to $150,000; 39% from $150,000 to $250,000; and 47% above $250,000.
  • 2.5% Wealth Tax: An annual tax on individual net wealth above $2 million, estimated to raise $6.59 billion annually. A couple pays nothing on combined net wealth up to $4 million. A companion trust tax is estimated to raise a further $0.11 billion.
  • 33% Capital Gains Tax: Applies to realised gains accruing after the tax begins, fully excluding the family home. Estimated annual revenue rises from a first-term average of $0.54 billion to $2.22 billion at year 10.
  • Financial Transactions Levy: A 0.1% levy covering equity and onshore foreign exchange turnover, estimated to raise $0.64 billion annually. Everyday household payments, wages, bills, and KiwiSaver contributions are strictly exempt.

Alliance Finance and Economy Spokesperson Quentin Findlay says the central focus of the policy is taxing wealth, not work.

“Aotearoa New Zealand currently taxes income from the very first dollar earned, while untaxed wealth multiplies without effort.

“The Alliance is offering a completely different set of priorities to provide working people and their families with security in a cost-of-living crisis.

“By shifting the tax burden onto those who already hold extensive wealth, an essential worker on $65,000 keeps an extra $2,408 every year. This is about ensuring our economy serves the people who actually do the work.”

ENDS

For more information contact Alliance Party Finance and Economy Spokesperson Quentin Findlay on Mobile 021 326 443

title.rendered: Alliance Calls for Universal Child Benefit

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party says current economic and social pressures highlight the need for meaningful cost-of-living relief and stronger support for young families, regardless of their background or employment status.

Alliance Party social welfare spokesperson and West Coast–Tasman candidate Sara Dyatlova-Murphy says many families are delaying having children, or having fewer children, because of the rising cost of living.

“Families should not have to choose between having children and being able to afford the basics. We need a system that provides reliable support to all families raising children,” Ms Dyatlova-Murphy says.

The Alliance supports the Child Poverty Action Group’s (CPAG) call to examine Working for Families and the In-Work Tax Credit.

“Targeted approaches such as these have created a two-tier system that can leave some of the families who need support the most without assistance,” Ms Dyatlova-Murphy says.

Families can miss out on the In-Work Tax Credit if they receive a main benefit or student allowance, or if they do not work enough hours. Families can also face unexpected overpayment bills when estimated weekly or fortnightly payments are reconciled at the end of the financial year.

“Working for Families and the In-Work Tax Credit are failing too many New Zealand families. Means testing creates unnecessary administrative costs and complexity, while support has not kept pace adequately with wages or done enough to reduce child poverty.”

The Alliance is campaigning to restore the Universal Child Benefit, with regular payments made to the main caregiver to help meet the costs of raising children.

“A universal payment would remove much of the complexity and administrative burden of the current system. It would give families less stress, greater dignity and greater financial security, allowing parents and caregivers to focus on raising happy, healthy children,” Ms Dyatlova-Murphy says.

The Alliance has also supported an immediate increase in all benefits, with regular indexation to average weekly earnings so that support does not fall behind the cost of living and wage growth.

Under the Alliance’s Universal Child Benefit proposal, payments would continue until each child turns 16.

“Every child deserves a secure start in life, and every family should have the support they need to provide it. A Universal Child Benefit is a simple, fair and effective way to make that happen,” Ms Dyatlova-Murphy says.

excerpt.rendered: The Alliance calls for a Universal Child Benefit to give every family reliable support and reduce the cost and complexity of raising children.

title.rendered: Alliance Party officially registered to contest 2026 General Election

content.rendered:
The Electoral Commission has officially approved the registration of the Alliance Party of Aotearoa New Zealand and its logo, clearing the way for the party to contest the nationwide party vote in the General Election on Saturday 7 November 2026.

The decision marks a major milestone in the relaunch of the party and means New Zealanders across the country will have the opportunity to cast a party vote for a democratic socialist alternative.

Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot says official registration clears the path for the Alliance to provide a strong and uncompromising voice for working people and those marginalised by the present system.

“Official registration confirms that the Alliance is back and will be campaigning for the party vote nationwide,” Mr Billot says.

“For too long, the working-class majority has been forced to choose between slight variations of the same status quo. The Alliance has returned to the political landscape to offer a clear and principled alternative focused on economic justice, workers’ rights and public ownership.”

Mr Billot says the party has built strong momentum since announcing its relaunch, with growing membership across Aotearoa and candidates stepping forward in key electorates.

He says the affiliation of the Maritime Union of New Zealand with the Alliance Party has also been a major game-changer, putting the political establishment on notice.

“People are hungry for real solutions to the cost-of-living crisis, decaying public infrastructure and underfunded public services.

“Our platform puts human needs before private profit. It calls for progressive tax reform, the return of key energy and transport assets to public ownership, free healthcare – including dental care – and a major state housing programme delivered through a re-established Ministry of Works.

“A party vote for the Alliance on 7 November will send a clear message that business as usual is unacceptable. We look forward to taking our campaign into communities throughout Aotearoa over the coming weeks.”

Background

The Alliance was founded in 1991 as a broad-left political party advocating social democracy, public ownership and workers’ rights. It entered Parliament in 1993 and served as the junior partner in the Labour–Alliance coalition government formed following the 1999 General Election. After a prolonged period of extra-parliamentary political activity, the party relaunched and is contesting the 2026 General Election as a democratic socialist alternative.

For more information contact Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot on 022 479 1786.

title.rendered: Alliance Party Announces Sara Dyatlova–Murphy as Candidate for West Coast-Tasman

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has announced software developer, community advocate, and mother Sara Dyatlova–Murphy as its candidate for the West Coast-Tasman electorate in the 2026 General Election.

Born and raised in Nelson with personal and family roots in Golden Bay, Motueka, Riwaka, and the West Coast, Ms Dyatlova–Murphy brings a rich blend of practical experience and grassroots organising.

Her background spans technology and software development alongside hands-on work in hospitality and seasonal fruit harvesting in local orchards.

Currently living in Riwaka as a stay-at-home mother, she understands the everyday pressures facing households across the region.

Her commitment to public advocacy is shaped by both local history and international perspective. Having experienced the harsh economic impact of the National Government’s 1991 “mother of all budgets” on households during her childhood, she later spent time living in Denmark, The Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and Australia.

Her time in Denmark demonstrated firsthand the high standard of security achieved through a well-funded social democracy.

Ms Dyatlova–Murphy says the West Coast-Tasman electorate is geographically large and diverse, but whether people live in Golden Bay, Motueka, or on ‘the Coast’, they all share common struggles.

“People across our region need access to timely healthcare, relief from cost-of-living pressures, affordable housing, and secure, well-paid jobs. As a mother, worker, and local resident, I am standing with the Alliance because I believe our communities deserve strong representation that fights for public ownership, workers’ rights, and a better future for our Tamariki.”

Ms Dyatlova–Murphy’s campaign will champion public services, disability rights, regional healthcare access, free education, public ownership of key assets, and economic security for regional workers.

Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot welcomed her candidacy.

“The Alliance is very happy to announce Sara Dyatlova–Murphy as the Alliance candidate for West Coast-Tasman,” he says.

“Sara brings real-world experience, deep roots across the region, and an unshakeable commitment to a better New Zealand. At a time when working families are bearing the brunt of economic pressure, Sara offers the practical, compassionate leadership we need.”

The Alliance Party extends its gratitude to previous candidate Louis Coup, who has stepped down from the race due to unavailability.

For more information contact Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot on 022 479 1786.

title.rendered: Alliance Backs Striking Department of Internal Affairs Workers

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has thrown its full support behind the 1,300 Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) workers who walked off the job today in a historic strike over fair pay.

Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot says these workers, whose work includes processing essential documents like passports and citizenship, are justified in taking collective action against an insulting 0.8% average pay offer.

“This is an effective pay cut during an ongoing cost-of-living crisis,” says Mr Billot.

“While everyday costs skyrocket, senior management and Government politicians are offering frontline staff crumbs.”

He says the industrial action comes immediately after an OECD report ranked New Zealand last among 37 developed nations for real wage growth, with Kiwi wages plummeting 6.4% below 2021 levels in real terms.

Mr Billot says the collapse of wage growth in New Zealand informs the same market data that employers will use to justify even lower pay offers further down the line.

“The Alliance Party knows that when workers fight for a better deal, they are fighting for a better deal for all workers.”

He says while DIA workers are told to tighten their belts, MPs enjoy regular, locked-in salary increases, padded by generous taxpayer-funded superannuation and accommodation subsidies.

“Likewise, public service chief executives routinely pocket salaries of hundreds of thousands of dollars a year.”

The Alliance calls on DIA management to return to the bargaining table and deliver a fair offer.

“The Alliance stands shoulder-to-shoulder with the DIA workers and their union, the PSA. Your fight is a fight for the collective wellbeing of all working-class New Zealanders.”

For more information contact Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot on 022 479 1786.

excerpt.rendered: The Alliance Party backs the 1,300 DIA workers striking over an insulting 0.8% average pay offer during a cost-of-living crisis.

title.rendered: Alliance Joins the Dots on Systemic Issues and Alleged Human Rights Abuses at Wakari

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party has expressed its strong concern at alleged grave misconduct found by inspectors in March at the inpatient unit of Wakari Hospital in Dunedin, with the closure of Ward 10A reported on Friday by Chief Ombudsman John Allen.

Reports by the inspectors revealed mistreatment of adults with intellectual disabilities that included long-term isolation, prolonged use of restraints, unlawful administration of medication, denying people access to their own money and individuals being incentivised for “good” behaviour with access to basic necessities, including the toilet and dental care.

Some cases could satisfy criteria under the international legal definition of torture, John Allen told RNZ’s Checkpoint. One reported case involved a person being secluded for eighteen months, and another strapped to an EVAC, causing carpet burns.

Alliance Party candidate for Taieri, Anna Knight, says the situation is “an appalling breach of human rights and dignity.”

She says while the decision from the Ministry of Health and Health New Zealand to close the ward for refurbishment was likely overdue, she shared community concerns that the relocation process may add further stress, with reports of some patients being moved out of the city in the interim.

Ms Knight says the review process now underway must ensure systemic failures are addressed, funding increased and accountability delivered.

“While the facility was underfunded and not fit-for-purpose, the dire situation in Ward 10A was clearly not solely due to its physical environment. The governance arrangements and clinical context must be scrutinised, so how and why this culture of cruelty was able to develop and continue unchallenged for so long can really sink in.”

“Our hearts go out to patients and their families, who will be devastated to hear of punitive and coercive treatment.”

“Think of the families who, already hesitant to place loved ones with complex needs into such facilities, but with few options available to them, eventually resign themselves to doing so, only to learn our healthcare system has actively failed them.”

One of the key concerns is how long these issues have gone unaddressed, despite repeated attempts to sound the alarm, including an OPCAT (Optional Protocol to the Convention Against Torture) inspection in May 2021.

Ms Knight says the Alliance supports the call from disabilities rights lawyer Huhana Hickey for a nationwide overhaul of the disability system.

Health NZ says it will continue working with patients, families, staff and unions throughout the transition.

Ms Knight says beyond existing unannounced inspections, one way to avoid the “unseen” proliferation of such malpractice would be if staff were better unionised and in touch with collegial best practice.

Healthcare unions must be strengthened so that their members’ concerns are heard and whistleblowers are able to report such issues as chronic understaffing without fear for their livelihoods, she says.

“We have to assume the majority of healthcare workers go into such industries because they are caring individuals. So somewhere along the line, they are feeling unsafe and corners are being cut on patients’ rights.”

“It is unacceptable that the trade-off for worker safety could effectively become torturing our most vulnerable. It’s not a mystery what the solutions are, the problem is the unwillingness to adequately resource them.”

For more information contact Alliance Party Taieri candidate Anna Knight on 020 4072 8703.

excerpt.rendered: Taieri candidate Anna Knight says the abuses uncovered in Ward 10A at Wakari Hospital are an appalling breach of human rights, and calls for systemic overhaul, funding and accountability.

title.rendered: Relaunched Alliance Party Announces First Auckland Public Meeting, Backed by Maritime Union and Former Cabinet Minister

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party will hold its first official public meeting in Auckland since its recent relaunch, signalling a bold return to the New Zealand political landscape.

Hosted by the Maritime Union of New Zealand (MUNZ) at their Auckland headquarters at the Okahu Bay Sports Club, the meeting will feature addresses from Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot and former Alliance Cabinet Minister Hon. Matt Robson, on Tuesday 7 July at 7pm.

Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot says the relaunch of the Alliance marks the revival of a crucial voice in New Zealand politics, with traditional left-wing principles focused on economic justice, public ownership, and strong worker protections.

“As political and economic pressures grow on regular New Zealanders, the Alliance is challenging the status quo and offering an unapologetic, principles-first alternative to the mainstream parties.”

Mr Billot says that the venue and the new partnership with the Maritime Union hold a strong symbolism.

“We are incredibly proud to hold our Auckland public meeting at the home of the Maritime Union, New Zealand’s oldest trade union with its nearly 150 years of struggle for the working class.”

“The Alliance is back because working people in New Zealand are being pushed to the brink. With its policies for proper funding of public health care, public ownership of key assets, and a major shift in tax policy to help the majority, the Alliance offers a plan, a path forward and hope.”

Mr Billot says the Alliance is building a genuine political alternative that puts people, public services, and workers’ rights back where they belong: as the top priorities.

Joining Billot on the stage is Hon. Matt Robson, whose previous tenure as a Minister in the 1999 Labour–Alliance coalition government brought vital progressive reforms to the justice system and international aid, as well as an important role in delivering paid parental leave and the establishment of Kiwibank.

His support for the relaunched Alliance represents a bridge between the party’s historic legacy and its future trajectory.

“The issues that brought the Alliance together originally have not gone away, in fact, they have intensified,” says Mr Robson.

“New Zealanders are looking for a political movement that stands for the democratic socialist values that built so much of value in our nation’s history. I am standing with Victor and the relaunched Alliance because we have a proven track record of achievements in this country, and it is time to do it again.”

All members of the public, community advocates, and media are warmly invited to attend.

Event details

  • What: The Alliance Party: First Relaunch Public Meeting
  • Speakers: Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot and former Cabinet Minister Hon. Matt Robson
  • When: Tuesday 7 July 2026, 7pm
  • Where: Okahu Bay Sports Club (MUNZ Auckland headquarters), 40 Reihana Street, Orakei, Auckland
  • Admission: Free, all welcome

For more information contact Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot on 022 479 1786 or Hon. Matt Robson on 021 909 936.

title.rendered: Alliance Party Welcomes Historic Affiliation of Maritime Union of New Zealand

content.rendered:
In an unprecedented advance for the political left in New Zealand, the Alliance Party has officially welcomed the formal affiliation of the Maritime Union of New Zealand (MUNZ).

The historic decision, formalised by the MUNZ National Council on 3 June in Wellington, unites one of the country’s most iconic and effective trade unions with the Alliance Party.

Under the new agreement, MUNZ will immediately take up a formal affiliation, including a voting position on the Alliance Party National Council.

Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot described the affiliation as a massive step forward for working-class politics in New Zealand.

“The affiliation of the Maritime Union to the Alliance is a game changer for the 2026 election and going forward, for advancing an uncompromising working class voice in New Zealand politics.”

“MUNZ has a proud, unbroken history, and this step aligns perfectly with the Alliance constitutional objectives of the democratic socialist principles of democracy, equality, and social ownership.”

Mr Billot says the Alliance will be campaigning in 2026 on economic resilience, infrastructure and KiwiWorks, a 21st-century Ministry of Works, all focused on supporting working people and their families.

He says the Alliance will also prioritise revitalising New Zealand shipping and rail, and keeping ports and infrastructure in public ownership.

“This affiliation is an acknowledgement of the MMP environment, and the Alliance is committed to working with other opposition parties to remove the Coalition Government.”

The Maritime Union will maintain its long-standing affiliation to the New Zealand Labour Party.

For more information, contact Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot on 022 479 1786.

Event details

  • When: Wednesday 3 June 2026, 7:40pm
  • Where: Thistle Hall Community Venue, 293 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington
  • Speakers: Victor Billot, Alliance Party Leader, and Josh Harford, Alliance candidate for Wellington North

For updates and attendance details, open the Facebook event.

title.rendered: Public Service Cuts a Direct Attack on New Zealand Workers

content.rendered:
Alliance Party media release
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Thursday 21 May 2026

The Alliance Party has condemned the Government’s escalating attack on public sector workers, warning that its continuing stream of public service cuts will deepen New Zealand’s economic and social crisis.

Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot says the Coalition Government’s agenda is actively worsening a severe, policy-driven downturn.

“Working-class people are being forced to pay the price for an economic crisis they did not create. The economy remains weak, families are under pressure, and the Government’s only response is to double down on failed austerity measures.”

Mr Billot says many families are now facing immense distress, including joblessness, poverty, and housing insecurity.

He says the Government is increasingly seen as a hostile force by ordinary New Zealanders because it is actively making people’s lives worse.

“The Government is fixated on cutting spending, laying off workers, squeezing the most vulnerable, and slashing, cancelling, and delaying desperately needed State housing construction.”

“This is a zombie resurrection of the brutal and disastrous neoliberal experiments of the 1990s.”

Mr Billot says starving public services and infrastructure will cause lasting damage to New Zealand.

“By the age of 30, around a quarter to nearly a third of New Zealand-born people are already living overseas. Destroying secure public sector jobs and opportunities will only accelerate this mass exodus of skilled and qualified workers.”

Mr Billot says lasting economic security requires a complete break from the failed neoliberal consensus.

“We do not have a wealth problem — we have a distribution problem.”

“We must urgently rebuild the power of the working class. Decades of anti-union attacks mean the benefits of production flow straight into the pockets of a wealthy ownership class, rather than into workers’ wages.”

“The Alliance stands in solidarity with public service workers and the wider working class. In 2026, we can end these attacks by an irresponsible Government made up of people who have no conscience and no understanding of the harm they are causing to working people.”

ENDS

For more information contact: Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot on 022 479 1786

title.rendered: Alliance Party Firmly Opposes “Backdoor Privatisation” of Kiwibank

content.rendered:
Alliance Party media release
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Wednesday 13 May 2026

Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot has condemned the Government’s renewed push toward the part-privatisation of Kiwibank.

Finance Minister Nicola Willis and State Owned Enterprises Minister Simeon Brown have been considering future capital-raising options, including a possible public listing or private-sector capital injection.

Mr Billot says the Alliance will fight any move to dilute public ownership of the bank.

“Kiwibank was established through the Alliance’s role in the Labour–Alliance Coalition Government to protect New Zealanders from the predatory profit-seeking of the overseas-owned banking system,” Mr Billot says.

“The Government is attempting to use manufactured fiscal constraints as an excuse to open up strategic public assets to private investors.”

Mr Billot says Kiwibank was never intended to be a vehicle for private profit but was designed to provide essential banking services for everyday New Zealanders and keep more of New Zealand’s banking profits in New Zealand.

“The Government should move its own banking business to Kiwibank,” Mr Billot says.

“Instead of looking to private investors for capital, the Government should allow Kiwibank to grow by using its own massive transaction volumes to strengthen the bank’s position.”

Mr Billot says the Alliance believes the state has an active responsibility to act as a direct provider and investor in essential economic infrastructure.

He says foreign investors already control a significant portion of New Zealand’s economy, with financial and insurance services making up a major share of foreign direct investment stock.

“A large part of the proceeds of New Zealanders’ work already leaves the country through interest, dividends and profits sent offshore,” Mr Billot says.

“The answer is not to further expose Kiwibank to the demands of private capital. The answer is to strengthen public ownership, public investment and democratic control.”

Mr Billot says fiscal sustainability should be pursued through economic sovereignty, equity and progressive taxation, not austerity or asset sales.

“Kiwibank belongs to the people of New Zealand, not the global market,” Mr Billot says.

“The Alliance remains committed to 100% public ownership and control of essential financial services like Kiwibank, so they operate in the public interest.”

ENDS

For more information contact: Alliance Party Leader Victor Billot on 022 479 1786

title.rendered: Alliance: Labour’s GP Loan Scheme Is A “Band-Aid” For A Broken System

content.rendered:
The Alliance Party says Labour’s Family Doctor Loan Scheme is a superficial fix for a primary care sector in structural collapse.

Alliance Party Health Spokesperson Ethan Gullery says more debt is not the solution for a failing funding model.

He says while Labour’s scheme acknowledges the crisis in primary care, lending money to GPs to buy into practices ignores the reality of how those practices function.

“Credit is not the problem,” says Mr. Gullery.

“The problem is a funding model that fails to reflect the real cost of keeping a community healthy. A GP who takes out a loan to buy a clinic is still operating under the same broken capitation formula the day they open the doors. The loan doesn’t change that.”

Mr. Gullery says Labour’s own campaign data acknowledges that one in six New Zealanders cannot afford to see a doctor. He says that the current “per-head” funding model penalises clinics in high-needs areas.

“A clinic in Linwood or Flaxmere managing high rates of diabetes, respiratory disease, and mental health complexity receives funding based on enrolled numbers, not on the reality of what those patients actually need,” says Mr. Gullery.

“The clinics doing the heaviest lifting are being pushed to the brink while GPs burn out and leave the profession.”

The Alliance is calling for a total overhaul of the system, moving away from the “small business” model toward a fully publicly funded Community Health Service.

Under the Alliance plan:

  • Salaried Professionals: GPs, Nurse Practitioners, and nurses would be salaried employees, not business owners, allowing them to focus entirely on patient care.
  • Integrated Care: Dental, optical, and mental health clinicians would be under one publicly funded model.
  • Streamlined Triage: Nurse Practitioners would handle first-contact appointments, while GPs focus on complexity and high-risk cases.
  • Prevention First: Practice nurses would lead chronic condition management to keep people out of hospitals.

“Poor oral health is a direct risk factor for dementia, and deferred GP visits become Emergency Department admissions,” says Mr. Gullery.

“Every dollar we fail to spend on prevention, we spend several times over on hospital care later. It is a fiscal no-brainer that successive governments, including Labour, have chosen to ignore.”

Mr. Gullery says Labour in Government neglected to address a two-tier employment market in healthcare by failing to include nurses working in primary care in nursing pay equity claims.

“The nurses holding our communities together are overwhelmingly women, yet they have been left out of pay equity settlements covering their hospital counterparts. This is a structural inequality Labour had every opportunity to fix.”

“New Zealand needs primary health care rebuilt as a public good. The Alliance has a plan to do exactly that.”
